title: ID0392232-DC/Si-D/AT[8qgG8Z] - PLC Communication Error + SafetyRelay_QA26
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
PLC Communication Error
SafetyRelay_QA26
EmergencyStopButton_SF2
DC4 didn't charge for 2 times with weird EcoG behavior
Root cause:
PLC Communication Error → Ethernet cable is damaged or faulty
SafetyRelay_QA26 + EmergencyStopButton_SF2→ Dispenser door switch is a bit damaged due to transport?
Solution:
Replace Ethernet cable
Close door “harder”
On DAMEX Sanctioned List:
Siemens
Warranty Status:
Active

additional_info.subject: ID0392232-DC/Si-D/AT[8qgG8Z] - PLC Communication Error + SafetyRelay_QA26 CRM:00315002111
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes,
Thank you for reaching out to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
Y2 / S9 313875948001
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
8qgG8Z
Problem Description
: Charger is not operational
Troubleshooting
:
After 2 long days we were able to bring back the charger to 99% operation. It seems there is still a pending issue but it's not critical. I will describe it afterwards.
When the dispenser was installed there was an error
Dispenser_PLC_A_KF201 - PLC Communication Error
,
SafetyRelay_QA26
and
EmergencyStopButton_SF2
.
For the communication error, I tried to reupload the TIA firmware to the PLC but it was not possible as it was not reachable due to a supposed QA210. Since that was not possible, you moved to site we tried to activate QA210. It was not possible because there was no problem with the TIA firmware, it was already toggled.
We moved on to the
most problematic error of the SafetyRelay+Estop
, we checked the whole circuit from the 24V emergency until we reached the FA12, on the part that we are connected to the dispenser we lost the 24V and as such we searched on the Dispenser door sensor, when we opened the sensor, the door sensor went back to operational and we lost the error flags. As such this must be due to the damaged that we found on the dispenser, caused the contacts to not be correct. So
this problem was fixed with closing the door with more force
.
For the
PLC Communication Error
, we could ping all the addresses via SSH but there were some packets lost. As such, we proceed to check via Network Scanner, from dispenser Switch → all okay we can see all the devices, and when we checked via main SiD, we couldn't see any of the dispenser IPs, which means that the problem is from the dispenser's switch to main charger.
After we replaced the Ethernet cable from SiD to dispenser the error was gone and we could charge in all outlets.
In the end you were able to notice one failed session in DC4. I couldn't get the full detailed information as I was busy with other tasks and couldn't fetch the DebugStation video.
Let's align on a schedule with the customer to trial again this Outlet as it's hard to proactively check the sessions. From what I see in the logs there were 2 successfull charging sessions followed by 2 that didn't work. We need to reproduce this error and what was the difference, is it possible that the cables could be also damaged in the transport and we can have a bad contact when plugging in.
For future reference, your ticket number is
0392232
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim
Please do not
change
the
subject of this Email when
replying
to it.

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0392232-DC/Si-D/AT[8qgG8Z] - PLC Communication Error + SafetyRelay_QA26 CRM:00315002111
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
The customer has unfortunately not yet test there new trucks.
Therefore, please keep the ticket open as the DC4 port still has a problem.
I would also like to mention that the door sensor issue was not resolved by closing the door more firmly from the dispenser, but by manually adjusting the locking mechanism (hook on the inside of the door).
As can be seen in the photo, the gap at the top is larger than at the bottom. Multiple attempts were made to close the door at the top, but the door could never be locked into place.
Additionally, I was informed by the factory that the issue with the LED strip (brightness inconsistency) should be reported to LV3.
The problem seems to be known.
Kind regards,
Johannes
